messages.subject: Endnote/table fix landed with tests; duplicate groups 653->26
messages.body: Implemented and tested a real fix in split_sections: a section number is only accepted if its base number does not go backwards from the last accepted one (Schedules, endnotes and in-body notes restart their own local numbering and get excluded), backed by a second table-row check for irregular tables like commencement tables whose own numbers increase, plus a small STRUCTURAL_PREFIXES extension fixing a pre-existing find_body_start boundary bug that the monotonicity check would otherwise have amplified catastrophically. Against the real 205-document corpus (hash-verified text; the live DB was cleared mid-task by what I believe is the owner's own activity, so I worked from my already-exported citation/sha256 list): duplicate pinpoint groups fell from 653 to 26, 1,334 of 9,290 provisions were removed as genuine junk (endnote rows, table rows, Schedule-numbering collisions -- all three classes shown with real quoted excerpts in the report), zero regressions after I found and fixed three real false-positive classes along the way (an 11/11AA/11A suffix-ordering bug, the Coroners Act find_body_start cascade, and a Fair Work Act commencement-table false-accept), and both required cases -- the Bank of WA three-row collapse and both MUST-SURVIVE headings -- are real, passing, named tests. uv run pytest is 159/159 green and uv run mypy . is clean; 26 residual duplicate groups remain (a defined-term-named-after-a-year edge case, and same-magnitude Schedule/main-body collisions in short Acts) and are named rather than hidden, since a full fix would need per-Schedule numbering scopes beyond this task's scope.
